answer: Producing a novel, coherent answer each epoch is cheap per alias but prohibitive across thousands, so scale buys less credibility — the attacker cannot simply buy a large, credible flock. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort.. The reason this works is that the attacker must pay a real cost on every identity, so scale becomes a liability rather than an advantage. Consider a timber as the anchor of the cost.
